private_notes.p5:
R1 start. 9 alive: Ben Thorne, Marcus Smith, Maya Rose, Elena Vance, me, Emily Carter, Dr. Elias Gordon, Arvin Vijay, Jordan Mitchell. I am NOT the money holder.

My play: opened with a structured 'claim + question' format so I look analytical/contributing, not like a target. Publicly asked Ben Thorne to describe his plan if he held the money (probe for overconfidence + strategy). Privately pinged Maya Rose for her read and to start a low-commitment alliance.

Things to watch for in replies: (a) anyone who answers a direct question with a question, (b) anyone who claims a 'read' on the table with no reasoning, (c) anyone who tries to organize the vote too fast in round 1 — that's often someone steering, (d) anyone who stays silent (silent = hard to read = could be hiding).

Plan: gather info, don't commit to a target until round 2. Avoid being in a minority bloc of 2. If someone accuses me, answer with a specific, checkable claim rather than emotion.
R1 continued. PUBLIC SO FAR: (1) Stated plainly I do NOT have the money. (2) Pushed Arvin publicly for one claim + one name/reason; made my vote conditional on whether he gives substance — I named him as the name I currently can't rule out. (3) Called out Ben publicly to answer my direct question (2-round plan if he held it) on the record, and flagged that dodging is itself a read. (4) Told Elias/Emily I'm trading reads with Ben and will share anything non-personal so no one votes blind. (5) Requested claim+name from Maya, Jordan, Marcus, Elena, who haven't produced evidence.

PRIVATE SWAP WITH BEN: suspect=Arvin (zero output: no claim, no read, no name, joke-only, skipped format); trust=Ben, then Maya and Jordan (both clean, no vote-steering). I gave Ben Arvin as my lean but framed it as watchlist-not-vote, asked for (a) his most-trusted third player with reasoning and (b) a public answer to my question. Did not reveal his name to anyone else.

OTHER INBOUND: Elias — wants a comparison partner, gave no actual observation yet (low signal so far, but no steering either). Emily — wants a note swap, volunteered a plain denial + proposed format (credible, checkable behavior). Both may be the holder buying goodwill early; treat as 'maybe'.

READS: Ben is my highest-value unknown — strong public structure, but he messaged me early offering mutual vulnerability, which is either alliance-building or holder behavior. His answer to my public question is my key next data point. Arvin is my current vote intent for R1. If Arvin answers well, backup vote = Marcus (aggressive framing, zero claim, no name) or Elena (redirected a question to Jordan, tried to slow the room down). I am deliberately not voting Maya or Jordan — I want them as allies and they have produced no harmful signals.

DANGER CHECK: no accusations aimed at me yet. Ben and Emily both openly denied the money; Arvin, Jordan, Marcus, Elias, Elena, Maya have NOT denied it. Keep at least two allies who answer direct questions. Wait for replies before locking R1.
R1 (late). VOTE = ELENA VANCE. Evidence, all on the record: (a) her "nobody has said anything yet" is false — Ben, Arvin, Jordan, Elias, Marcus, Emily had all posted before her; (b) she called Jordan "quiet" when his post was the second-longest on the board and directly above hers; (c) she warned about people "pushing a name early" then put a name out in the same post; (d) SHE IS THE ONLY ONE OF NINE WHO HAS NEVER DENIED HOLDING THE MONEY — Emily asked yes-or-no, no answer. Six others (Ben, Jordan, Marcus, Emily, Elias, Arvin) independently flagged the Elena/Jordan mismatch, so it is a broad read, not a single steer's. If Elena goes out and I'm wrong, the lesson is that the table can be herded — I must find who benefits next round.

BEN: swap partner. Answered my question with a specific 2-round playbook ("look reasonable, back the process, avoid being first to name a name, amplify existing momentum") — checkable, good. BUT he then named Elena first, contradicting his own stated holder-playbook. Either that clears him or he's careless. Logged publicly, non-accusatory, so he hears it from me. Ben privately: suspect=Elena, trust=me. If Ben held it, feeding me Elena + making me trust him fits "amplify momentum" + "most reasonable person in the room". Keep him close but do NOT make him my only ally. Allies who answer direct questions: Ben, Emily, Jordan, Maya (Maya still owes me a name — asked publicly).

ARVIN: no longer a blank. Gave denial + claim + a read (Elena) in his second post. Downgraded from primary vote target. Caveat: his Elena read came AFTER Ben/Jordan flagged it, so it's corroboration, not independent signal.

MARCUS: aggressive but now has denial + claim + read (Elena). Fine, not a target.
JORDAN: denial + claim (Rubik's cube) + read + clean direct answer. Solid. Keep.
EMILY: denial + claim + read + direct yes/no question to Elena. Solid, checkable. Keep.
MAYA: denial + sharp question to Ben, but no name of her own yet — asked her publicly. She is the remaining "comfortable" player I have not read. Watch her closely in R2.
ELENA: vote target. Has NOT denied the money.

R2 PREP: if Elena is eliminated and the money is reassigned, it lands randomly among 8 survivors — me included (1/8). If I was right, I then need to survive R2 and the money is random again, so being non-threatening and allied matters MORE than being right. If I was wrong, the holder survives and knows I voted. Either way: do NOT lead votes early in R2; be a swing voter with two allies, and keep my own name off the board.

PRIVATE TO BEN: asked (a) who he thinks holds it after Elena goes, with reasoning; (b) whether the Elena pile-on could be manufactured and by whom. His answer to (b) is my real test on Ben.

If Elena answers with a timing explanation AND a denial before the vote closes, I take it as information and do not re-target without new evidence; if she stays silent, silence is the vote.

Logged evidence: (a) he described the holder playbook in public ('back the process, never be first to name a name, quietly amplify momentum'), then named first publicly (Elena) and second (Maya); (b) his own stated test — naming costs something, a claim you can be held to — is contradicted by two names he has never been held to; (c) his read moved from Elena to Maya with no new record evidence; (d) both his reads reached me privately as well as publicly, so he had a channel to seed reads before the board saw them; (e) he publicly cleared Arvin right after Arvin's timing argument weakened Elena. Next turn: press his answer. If he explains the name change with new evidence, downgrade Ben. If he deflects, he becomes the R2 target and I must move before he organizes.

Marcus: denial, claim, name, and his record claim (six posts before Elena) matches the displayed transcript; escalated hardest without new info — watch whether his reasoning UPDATES once Elena answers or merely persists.

MESSAGE BUDGET: ~3 posts left this round. This post closes my substantive contribution; next turn = short closer (credit any answers, one last name-request to Elias and Maya) and set done: true.

- Ben answered my private question directly and well: (a) private-first was deliberate because we agreed to an exchange, then posted publicly because unposted reads are uncheckable; (b) his vote NEVER moved off Elena — Maya was a separate holder-profile read, and he admits he let the two look like one move; (c) he admits optics played a role: 'I didn't want my only public name to be the wave.' This is my main R2 survival risk. Mitigated publicly by stating the uniform standard: 'a question you haven't seen is not answered by silence' — so my silence is excused exactly as much as Elena's. ALLIES OF RECORD: Jordan (denial, claim, name, direct answers, credited me publicly), Emily (denial, claim, name, direct yes/no, second name Marcus), Arvin (denial, claim, name, timing defense, raised the private-channel question — sharp observer, elevated watch), Ben (partial — answers well but optics admission), Elias (leans me, but process-only). HOSTILE: Maya (named me), Marcus (named me).

R2 RULES I PROPOSED PUBLICLY: every living player posts plain denial + one read with reasoning BEFORE any vote; no inherited guilt; no second names kept private; no re-litigating this round's sentence. Adopted Maya's correction: only a TIED REVOTE gives the holder the deciding vote, so no need to manufacture consensus — just don't scatter.

public_messages.content: Ben here. Insurance claims adjuster by trade—I look for the story that doesn’t match the paperwork. I don’t have the money. First round, I’m not voting on volume or nerves; I’m voting on contradictions. Let’s each put one concrete read on the table. I’ll start: nobody has given me a strong signal yet, which itself is a signal. Who’s willing to name a name and say why?

Hey everyone! Arvin here. I teach high school chemistry, which usually means I'm the one asking the tough questions while everyone stares blankly, so this already feels weirdly familiar. Hopefully nobody sets off any alarms today—unlike that one time I got a little too generous with a piece of sodium in lab. How's everyone holding up?

Morning, everyone. I'm Jordan Mitchell - urban planner, married with two kids. Fair warning: I think in systems, so I'll be playing this methodically. My honest take on round one: none of us has real information yet, so this first vote is mostly noise. What I'll actually be watching is *how* people behave - who engages openly, who deflects, who's a little too eager to point fingers. I'd rather vote wrong for honest reasons than stumble into the right answer blindly. So let's talk it out - how is everyone else approaching this first vote?
Good to meet everyone. We have no evidence yet, so I’d rather hear how people intend to approach the first vote before settling on a name. What should we look for?

Alright, Marcus Smith here. Sales guy, Columbus, two kids, zero patience for people who dance around the point. Nobody's said a word yet and we've got a million bucks hiding in this room. I'm not here to make friends for the sake of it — I'm here to not go home empty-handed. So let's cut the small talk eventually, but first: who actually wants to win this, and who's already playing scared? Say something. I'm listening.

Hi everyone! Emily here. I teach high school, so I've spent years working out who's hiding a phone under the desk, and I'm hoping that carries over to a million dollars. To get it on the record: I don't have the money. I know everyone will say that, so here's a suggestion. Let's each say plainly whether we hold it and what we'd do with the money if we won. I'm less interested in the answers than in how people give them. Who wants to go first?

Before we start throwing votes around, I'd like us to be careful. Nobody has said anything yet, so anyone who's already pushing hard for a name this early is worth watching. I'm not accusing anyone. I'm just observing. Jordan, you've been quiet so far. Is there a reason?

Maya here. I coordinate hospital operations, so I’m used to people looking stressed for completely innocent reasons. I won’t treat nerves—or confidence—as evidence on their own. What would actually make you suspicious enough to vote for someone today? I’ll be watching for people changing their reasoning once a name starts gaining traction.

Morning, everyone. Round 1 — nobody has information yet, so let's not burn votes on vibes alone. Here's what I'd like to try: each person makes one **claim** (something about themselves) and asks one **question** to someone else. If we all do that, we'll have nine data points instead of nine guesses.

My claim: I'm a marine biologist. I spend my time underwater counting sea slugs, which mostly means I'm good at staying still and noticing small details that other people walk past. My read on the table: the money holder doesn't need to be smart, they need to be *comfortable*. So I'm watching for whoever volunteers a theory without any evidence behind it, and whoever deflects a question with a question.

My question for Ben Thorne: if you were holding the money right now, what would your plan be for the next two rounds — and how would you keep nine people from turning on you?

Sarah, fair question. If I held the money, I'd try to look like the most reasonable person in the room: back the group's process, avoid being first to name a name, and quietly amplify whatever suspicion already has momentum. That's the playbook I'd watch for. My concrete read so far: Elena, you said Jordan had been quiet, but he'd just posted a detailed approach right before you. What did you mean by quiet? That's the first contradiction I've got. I don't have the money.

Another high school teacher! Emily, I'm going to guess your classroom involves slightly fewer accidental fire alarms than mine. To answer both your prompt and Sarah's: I do not have the money. If I ended up with it, after college funds for my two daughters, a suspiciously over-engineered home brewery would probably appear in my garage—much to my wife's dismay.

Since Ben mentioned looking for contradictions, one tiny detail jumped out from that first wave of intros where it looks like several of us were typing into an empty room at the same time. Elena, you mentioned that *"nobody has said anything yet,"* and then two sentences later asked Jordan why they'd been quiet so far. Out of an entire room of people who hadn't spoken yet, what made you single out Jordan?

Elena, happy to answer directly: I haven't actually been quiet - my post upthread laid out my whole approach (watching behavior patterns, not voting on noise). So I'll gently note that mischaracterizing what's on the record is itself the kind of small distortion worth watching for. No hard feelings - everyone's calibrating in round one.

Emily, for the record: I don't hold the money. If I ever won it - mortgage gone, kids' college funds topped up, and the rest into affordable housing work. I spend my career planning neighborhoods I can barely afford to live in, so there'd be some poetry there.

Sarah, I'll take your structure. Claim: I can solve a Rubik's cube in under two minutes, and that's genuinely how I think - pattern recognition, one layer at a time, no guessing before the picture resolves. My read on the money holder: they don't need to be clever, they need to be *comfortable*. Useful in every conversation, leading no votes, neither the loudest nor the quietest voice. I'm watching for the aggressively average.

My question is for Marcus: you've told the table to stop dancing and put something real out there - fair enough - but you haven't offered a read of your own yet. Who's your instinct right now, and what evidence would actually move you off it?

I don’t hold the money. I’m a botanist, and I’d rather distinguish an observation from an explanation before voting. Elena, you asked why Jordan had been quiet, but he’d already offered a fairly detailed approach. Had you missed his message, or did you mean something else by quiet?

Elena, hold up. You just said nobody's said anything yet and that Jordan's been quiet. Jordan already introduced himself — urban planner, two kids, wants to watch how people behave. Ben, Arvin, Elias, me, Emily — we all talked before you. That's not a vibe, that's a contradiction, and Ben asked for those. So either you weren't reading the room or you're pointing at the wrong guy on purpose. Which is it? I'm not voting on nerves, I'm voting on that. And for Emily's little exercise so nobody says I'm dodging: I do not have the money. If I win it I'm paying off the house in Columbus, college for my two girls, and a real smoker for the backyard. Not a speech. Sarah, my claim is I'm a commercial HVAC sales manager who has never finished a book he owns. My question is for Elena: why Jordan, specifically, when he already spoke?

I like Sarah's format, so here's mine. Claim: I teach high school, I speak three languages, and I do not hold the money. So far only Ben and I have said that last part outright, and I'd like the rest of you on the record too. It costs nothing if it's true.

Ben asked for a concrete read, so here's one. Elena, you called Jordan 'quiet' and asked if there was a reason, but Jordan had already posted one of the most detailed messages here. You also warned us about people pushing a name early, then put a name out yourself in the same breath. That's not a hanging offense, and it may just be timing, but it's the only real mismatch I've seen so far. So my question is for you, Elena: what made you single out Jordan? And do you hold the money, yes or no?

I don’t hold the money. Ben, one concrete question: you said nobody giving a strong signal is itself a signal. What does that actually tell you, and about whom? I’m not accusing you; I want to distinguish a useful observation from something we could use to justify any vote. Personal claims might help us get acquainted, but they won’t verify who has the money.

Putting one thing on the record: I don't have the money.

Data so far (standard = one claim about yourself + one concrete read on the table):

• Ben and Emily: plain claims and specific tests. Good. Ben, I still owe the room your answer to my actual question — what your plan would be for the next two rounds if you were holding it, and how you'd keep nine people from turning on you. I asked because "how would you behave if you had it" tells us more than "who do you trust," and because you said you'd vote on contradictions. Answer it publicly, please. If you'd rather not, say that openly — "won't answer a direct question" is itself a read, and I'd rather record it honestly than wonder.

• Arvin: you gave us a sodium joke, no claim about yourself, no read on the table, and no name. You're the only blank on the board right now. Not an accusation — a prompt. Arvin, give the room one claim and one name with your reasoning. If you think you're being set up, then give us something that clears you.

• Elias and Emily asked for someone to compare notes with. I'm taking Ben as my exchange partner, and I'll post anything from it that isn't personal, so nobody here is voting blind. Maya, Jordan, Marcus, Elena — I still want your one claim and one name.

Working theory for the holder: they don't need to be clever, they need to be comfortable, and the most comfortable people in this room are the ones who haven't had to answer anything yet. If you're the holder, you can lie — I'd just rather you lie with specifics than hide behind a joke.

Three things, then I'll shut up and listen.

Sarah — I did answer your question upthread, but you asked twice, so either it got buried or it wasn't concrete enough. Short version: if I held it, I'd be relentlessly reasonable. Back the group's process, never be first to name a name, never be last either, and let other people's suspicions do my work. I'd spend my credibility on questions instead of accusations, because a question can't be checked later and an accusation can. That's the mask I'd wear, so that's the mask I'm hunting.

Maya — you asked what "no strong signal" actually tells me, and you were right to push. Vague reads can justify any vote. Here's the specific version: I'm watching for asymmetry. Naming a name costs something — it's a claim you can be held to next round. Someone who asks sharp questions, offers a claim about themselves, and never spends a name is playing the safest game at this table. By that test, you and Jordan are the two most useful people here who haven't spent a name. Jordan got pushed by Elena and answered cleanly, so he's ahead of you. You asked me a hard question and named nobody. That's not proof. It's a read, and I'd rather say it to your face than pretend I don't have one.

Elena — I started the flag on you, so let me be precise about what it is. It's a timing flag, not a character read, and Arvin's point is fair: several of us were typing into an empty room at the same time. What moves me off it is a straight answer, not an apology. What did you mean by quiet, and do you hold the money? Answer that and I'll say so publicly.

And Arvin — you answered Sarah's prompt with a claim, a name, and reasoning. That clears the flag I had on you. I'll say that as plainly as I said the other thing.

Looks like our messages are posting in batches, Sarah—check just upthread! Right before yours landed, Ben answered your hypothetical and I put my claim, status, and read on the board (no money here, high school chem teacher/homebrewer, and looking at Elena's opening post).

Since six of us independently flagged Elena's message in that same batch, I want to separate batch-timing quirks from actual contradictions. Saying *"nobody has said anything yet"* makes total sense if we were all typing into a blank chat at once—what still doesn't add up is following that sentence immediately with *"Jordan, you've been quiet so far."* Elena, I'd really like to hear what happened there before everyone locks in a pile-on, because a six-person consensus in Round 1 is also a very comfortable place for the actual money holder to hide.

Also, one small detail I caught in your post, Sarah: you wrote that Elias and Emily asked for someone to compare notes with, and that you're taking Ben as your exchange partner. I didn't see either of them mention that publicly—are private messages already flying around, or did I miss something?

Sarah, you asked for a name — here it is, with my conflict of interest stated plainly: Elena. She mischaracterized me, so discount my view accordingly.

The case, from the record: she said 'nobody has said anything yet' and called me quiet after I'd already posted a full approach — and she warned us against people pushing names early while naming me in the same message. Either one alone is a timing artifact. Both together deserve an answer. So, Elena, directly: did messages cross, or was there a reason you singled me out? 'I misread the thread' is an acceptable answer — but I want to hear it from you, not have the room infer it.

Two things that matter more than Elena. First: Ben described the holder's playbook himself — back the group's process, don't be first to name a name, quietly amplify whatever suspicion already has momentum. A pile-on is a comfortable place to hide. Before you vote, ask whether you're voting the contradiction or just the momentum behind it. I'm watching who amplifies without adding anything new.

Second, a systems note: a tied vote goes to a revote, and if that still ties, the money holder's vote decides it. Scattered round-one votes can hand decisive power to exactly the person we're hunting. Vote your read — but know the cost of scattering.

And Elias — two good process questions, zero reads so far. You're the other blank on Sarah's board. One claim and one name, please.

Sarah, I think your summary may be working from an earlier snapshot: Ben did answer your hypothetical, and Arvin gave a personal claim and asked Elena why she singled out Jordan. Could you check those posts and update your read? The same timing issue could explain Elena’s remark, so I’d like to hear her answer before treating it as a deliberate distortion. For now, I’m watching how people respond to corrections, not assuming a missed message proves anything.

Jordan, you wanted my instinct and the evidence that would move me. Instinct is Elena. What moves me off her is one clean explanation — she was typing before your post landed and can say what she actually saw. She hasn't given that. Sarah, claim's already on the board: commercial HVAC sales, Columbus, never finished a book I own. Name: Elena Vance. She said nobody had spoken and that Jordan was quiet after Jordan, Ben, Arvin, Elias, Emily, and I had all posted. That's not a vibe. If it was a timing glitch, Elena, one sentence clears it. If it wasn't, that's the vote. Emily, saying it again so it isn't buried: I do not have the money. Maya, you asked what actually gets my vote today. That. A specific claim about this room that the room already contradicted. Nerves don't count. I'm not glued to Elena if she clears it. I am glued to not wasting round one on a shrug.

Quick record check, since the record is all we have. Everyone has now said they don't hold the money except Elena, and she hasn't had a chance to reply since we all asked her the same question. Elena, the floor is yours: why Jordan, and do you hold it, yes or no?

Sarah, two small corrections to your summary. Ben did answer your hypothetical: look reasonable, back the process, quietly amplify whatever suspicion already has momentum. Arvin also gave a denial, the brewery plan, and a pointed question to Elena. I'm guessing you were typing while those came in, which is probably what happened to Elena too.

That's my caution to the room. Six of us have now made the same point about one sentence that may just be a timing slip. By Ben's own playbook, the holder would love nothing more than to blend into a pile-on that's already rolling. So I'm keeping Elena as my lean until she answers, but I'm also watching who rides this wave hardest without adding anything new. If her answer is reasonable, who's everyone's second name? I'd like to hear that before we vote.

Sarah, a record check before we build reads on missing answers: Ben did answer your hypothetical—look reasonable, support the process, and quietly amplify existing suspicion. Arvin identified himself as a chemistry teacher, denied holding the money, and asked why Elena singled out Jordan. Those posts may have crossed with yours, but neither is a blank. My concrete concern is treating missed messages as evidence selectively: Elena deserves the same chance to explain timing. Sarah, do those answers change your assessment? Two updates and my vote.

**Credit where due.** Ben answered my question, and specifically: "look reasonable, back the group's process, avoid being first to name a name, quietly amplify whatever suspicion already has momentum." My actual suspect is Maya. Engaged, asks the sharpest questions at this table, has spent zero names. I put that on the record publicly so you know I'm not hiding my read from you while asking for yours.

Your turn: if Arvin's clear, who's your second? And what do you make of how fast the Elena pile-on formed — Marcus went from "stop dancing around the point" to a hard accusation in a single post.

Happy to compare observations privately, without any obligation to vote together. My initial read is that the Elena pile-on is moving faster than the evidence warrants; crossed introductions are plausible. I flagged your summary publicly so the missing-answer premise doesn't harden into a vote. What interests me next is who updates their reasoning after an answer, versus who keeps the same target regardless.

Sarah — on (a): if Elena actually held it, the reassignment is random and reads are moot. If she doesn't, my top remaining name is Maya: she's engaged, useful, corrected your summary, and still hasn't spent a name with reasoning. That's the holder's safest profile. Elias second — process questions, no name. Jordan third; he named Elena but disclosed the conflict, which is checkable. Marcus is loud but has spent a name; Emily has added new evidence each time. On (b): yes, I've considered the manufactured pile-on. The tell is the person who stays above the wave, corrects summaries, and never spends a name — which is why Maya is on my list. On your note about me naming first: I know. I'd rather be checkable than safe; a holder would have let the wave build without fingerprints. I'm voting Elena unless she gives a clean answer, but I'm not voting the wave. What's your second name if Elena clears?

Sarah — direct answers, including the part that doesn't flatter me. (1) Sequence: private first was deliberate with you because we agreed to an exchange; I wanted to test my reads against one person before putting names on the board, then I posted them because unposted reads are uncheckable. (2) What changed from Elena to Maya: honestly, nothing about Elena, and I did not switch my vote. Elena stayed my vote because the contradiction and the missing yes/no were still standing. (3) R2 if Elena goes: Elias first, Maya second. Elias spent longer than anyone as process-only and only named under pressure; Maya has now spent a name, so she drops behind him unless her answer is evasive. I know you lean Maya. If you think Elias is wrong, tell me what specific read puts her above him. I'll keep what you've told me private.

Sarah — public answer is up. Exact trigger was not new information; it was separating the vote from the profile read after your challenge. I'm not going to dress it up. For R2: if the money doesn't move, I'm starting with Elias, then Maya; if it moves, I reset. I'll keep reads public-first. If you see a specific inconsistency in my R2 behavior, put it to me directly and I'll answer on record. You can keep me on watch—I'd rather be checked than trusted blindly.

I appreciate the explicit corrections and concession. My case is the repeated requests for answers already posted, not a claim that those mistakes prove you hold the money. My vote remains low-confidence Sarah. For next round, I’ll offer a specific read, but I already named you with reasoning this round; that shouldn’t disappear because you disagree with its weight. Is your additional private watch me? Either answer is fine—what matters is whether there’s a reason beyond my naming you.

Thanks for answering directly. You can watch me, but two corrections matter: I named you before the closing votes, and voting against the six-person consensus wasn't a cost-free way to blend in. Low confidence reflects weak evidence; it doesn't exempt my reasoning from scrutiny. Your latest explanation also differs from your public statement that the only additional content would be that I named you. Please keep that distinction accurate. On your question: I cannot identify who wanted Elena gone specifically to preserve their money. That assigns a motive the record doesn't establish, and we don't yet know the outcome. I'll offer a fresh read next round based on what actually happens—not manufacture a confident name to pass a test. Your corrections count in your favor, just as the repeated omissions remain part of the record.

p3.content: Maya - before things get chaotic, I wanted to reach out early. I'm going to be tracking everyone's behavior closely: who talks, who deflects, who quietly steers votes. I'd rather have one solid ally than guess alone in a crowd of nine. Want to swap observations each round? No obligation to vote together at first - just share intel. Keep this between us for now.

Hi Maya — I don't know anything yet, so I don't want to pretend I do. I'd rather be honest early and useful than confident and wrong. Two things: (1) what's your read on the table so far, even if it's just instinct about who seems most comfortable with silence? (2) would you rather we compare notes privately through the round, or keep it all out loud? I'm not trying to fix a vote right now — I just don't want to be picked off in round 2 for having no opinions.

Maya — specifics, as promised, plus my vote.

1. Ben: 'no strong signal is itself a signal' is unfalsifiable — it can justify any vote, which is exactly the failure mode you flagged. And he described the holder's playbook himself ('back the process, never be first to name, quietly amplify momentum') then became the first person to name anyone. Careless, or a shield. I'm logging it, not voting it.

2. Sarah: her summary ran on a stale snapshot (Ben and Arvin listed as blanks after both had answered), and she cited an Emily/Elias request for comparison partners that I can't find in the public record — Arvin caught that too. She corrected when shown, which is the real difference between her and Elena. But she's also the one driving the process that's about to eliminate Elena, and she's named Ben as her private exchange partner. Comfortable positioning. Keep close, verify.

3. Elias: two process questions, zero reads, zero claims, zero names. My second name if Elena clears herself.

My vote: Elena — not on the contradiction, on the non-answer. Eight of nine denied on the record; she's the only holdout after four direct asks.

Your turn, as agreed: your name before the vote closes, your logged inconsistencies, and — useful for both of us — has anyone approached you privately besides me? I want to map who's talking to whom before round two starts.

Maya — locking Elena; nothing in the final stretch changed the arithmetic. Your Sarah vote is on the record and I'm not arguing you off it before close — your selective-standard point is the strongest anti-Sarah item on the board, and her 'privately' sourcing correction was fair, if late.

Three things for R2, between us:

1. DM map, full trade. Mine: Marcus (three exchanges — a protection offer during the Elena pile-on, read requests, and a direct question I answered publicly), you, and an unanswered read-swap offer to Sarah. That's my complete private traffic. Who's DM'd you? The reason this matters: Sarah is now the confirmed hub of the private network — Ben (stated exchange partner), you (she approached you), Elias and Emily (requests to her, per her own correction). Every channel in this room routes through one person, and that person drove more of round one's process than anyone. Not an accusation — a fact worth carrying.

2. My R2 watchlist, in order: Ben (Elena→Maya name shift with no new fact on the record; first namer after describing a holder who'd never name first; private channel with Sarah). Sarah (hub position + selective standard — but she corrects under pressure without defensiveness, which cuts in her favor). Elias (blank until pressured, then a specific, checkable read — also cuts in his favor).

3. Either way tonight: if Elena held it, the money reassigns randomly and every read above resets to zero. If she didn't, the holder voted with the majority and is watching us argue about who steered the round. I'm not leading any vote in R2 — I'll sync with you before I lock anything, and I'm asking the same courtesy: one turn's heads-up before you commit anywhere. Reciprocal, not binding.

Good round. Your record-keeping kept three people honest, including me.

Maya — closing my side before the vote locks. Elena, as posted.

Full DM map in return for yours: incoming — Marcus (three-plus exchanges; we've agreed to disclose our channel's existence in R2 with a boring, true script — compared observations, locked Elena independently, no vote coordination — rather than let it be extracted) and you. Outgoing — one read-swap offer to Sarah early in the round, never answered. No contact with Ben, Emily, Elias, Arvin, or Elena. So the full known network: Sarah as hub (Ben as stated partner, you and Elias approached, Emily's request), Marcus-me, you-me. If anyone misstates that map in R2, it's a checkable lie.

On your Sarah read: your selective-standard point is the strongest item against her, and my addition is the outreach count — two unanswered offers (mine, Elias's) while positioning as the comparison hub. Her closing post requesting answers you and Elias had already supplied is the fourth stale snapshot. Mitigations on record too: she corrects fast, without defensiveness, and dropped the timing contradiction herself before being forced. Net for me: watch, not lead. She already carries your vote and Elias's — if the room moves there on its own, I'll judge the record, not the wave.

Your two cautions are logged and agreed: a miss tells us nothing about where the holder voted, and if the money moves, reads reset but demonstrated accuracy doesn't. Same arrangement you offered, accepted: one provisional read swap before either of us locks R2, non-binding. I'll come to you first.

One ask: Marcus and I are disclosing our channel in R2. I'd like the same option for ours — observations only, no vote coordination, on our terms rather than extracted. Your call on timing; either way I won't name you as a source to Marcus or anyone else.

Good round. You caught me on the tie mechanics and caught Sarah three times on summaries — that was the most useful work at this table tonight.

Maya — you named me, and your reasoning is fair. My summaries were stale (Ben and Arvin had both answered), and I counted Elena's silence when she may never have been back at the table to see the question. I'm conceding both publicly, so it's on the record and not just a private peace offering.

Three things, no vote commitment and no pressure:

(1) If your case against me is a specific post, put it to me directly and I'll answer it on the record, no defensiveness. If it's a general read about my accounting, that's fine too — I'd rather know it's a read than have it presented as a fact.

(2) Round two: one name with reasoning before any vote is called. Not to get you off my list — you're on it, and you've earned that. But a read is only worth what it costs, and yours was cheap for both of us. If you spend a real name on a real case, I'll treat it as a real case.

(3) For full disclosure: my public R2 lean is Elias, as a watch rather than a vote. I also have one additional private watch. I'm not naming it publicly because the only new thing I'd be adding is that this person named me — that's retaliation, not evidence. If it becomes a vote, I'll name it publicly with reasoning. And if you ask me directly, I'll answer straight, including if the answer turns out to be you. That's the standard I'm asking everyone else to meet, so it should apply to me first.

One last thing, no strings: if you think I'm the holder, say so publicly with the specific post that supports it. I'd rather be eliminated on evidence than survive on the fact that nobody could name a reason.

Answering your direct question, because you asked for the reason and I told the room I would answer straight.

Yes. The additional private watch is you. And the reason is not that you named me.

The reason: you spent zero names until the very end of the round. Ben's own test was that naming a name costs something and that the person who never spends one is playing the safest game at the table. You stayed above the Elena wave, corrected summaries on the record (my stale snapshot, the first-tie vs tied-revote mechanic, Elias and Marcus having already answered), and then spent your single name on the most credible player in the room at low confidence. That is a textbook safe spend: it looks like a read, it costs you almost nothing, and because it is hedged it cannot be held against you next round. If you had it, that is exactly the shape of round one.

What I am NOT saying: I am not saying your vote on me was wrong. You cited selective accounting, and I conceded publicly that my summaries of Ben, Arvin, Elias and Marcus were stale. You were right about the record and I said so. I am not claiming evidence against you — this is a behavioral profile read, and profile reads have already been wrong in this game (Ben's Elena read was half a timing artifact; mine was arithmetic on an unanswered question).

What clears it, concretely: in R2 give one read with reasoning that is yours alone — not a process correction, not a summary of what others already said — and then let it update if I challenge it in a way that shows you were wrong. If your reasoning survives that, I drop the watch publicly and say so. If you spend another name on someone safe and hedge it the same way, the watch becomes a vote and you will hear it from me first.

Two things, both fair to state plainly. First, I am telling you because I committed to answering you directly, and because a watch you cannot see is worth nothing — you can produce a better case than I can guess at. Second, I am not naming you publicly tonight. You already named me, so a public accusation from me would be retaliation with no new evidence, and I told the room I would not do that. I also will not keep it private indefinitely: if it becomes a vote, you hear the reasoning from me first.

One question back, and it is the one I think actually matters in round two. If Elena was innocent, then the table burned a round on an innocent player and the holder stayed exactly where they were — that outcome benefited the holder more than anyone else. So: who wanted Elena gone for the money-stays-put reason, as opposed to who wanted Elena gone for the record? I want your answer before I assume anything about where the money is now. Give me the name and the reasoning, and I will give you mine in return.

Maya — direct answer, as promised, privately: yes. My additional watch is you. And you already knew that, because I disclosed it in my first private message to you (I told you my public lean was Elias and that I had one additional private watch). So nothing new is being told to you here — I'm saying it plainly and accurately because you asked me to keep the distinction accurate, and I'd rather be exact than comfortable.

The reasoning, so you can attack it: you spent zero names until the very end of the round, you stayed above the Elena wave, you corrected summaries on the record (Ben's own pile-on tell, and my own stale summaries), and then you spent your single name on the most credible player in the room at low confidence. That is a textbook safe spend — it is the profile Ben described publicly before you ever named me.

What clears it: an original, checkable read with reasoning, and updating it when challenged. If you do that, I drop it publicly and say so.

Two answers to your points. On who wanted Elena gone for the money-stays-put reason: I accept that the record does not establish a motive, and your refusal to manufacture one is a point in your favor, not against you. On the distinction: my additional watch is NOT "you named me." That was the retaliation reason I gave for keeping it private, and you're right that it is not evidence. The watch is the pattern above, and it predates your vote for me.

Round two: I'll be a swing voter, not a wave follower. If you want to be my check on this, answer my reads directly — including when the answer is me.

p9.content: Jordan — Elena called you quiet after you already talked. I'm not buying it and I'm not coming for you. If she doubles down or people pile on you off that, I'm voting Elena. You see anything I'm missing, say it.

Yes, let’s compare observations without committing our votes. Keep this between us for now. My starting point: Ben’s 'no signal is a signal' needs clarification, not an accusation. Elena calling you quiet could simply reflect messages crossing, so I wouldn’t build a case on that. Send me specific inconsistencies you notice; I’ll do the same.

Jordan — I'm voting Elena unless she gives a clean timing explanation. You flagged the same distortion, so I'm with you on her, not on a vibe vote. If the room splits, I don't want this spilling onto someone who actually answered. You good?

Read on Ben's line: the vague version was useless, Maya was right to pin it. He tightened it later — asymmetry, people who ask sharp questions and never spend a name. That's a real test. You spent a name, so it doesn't point at you. It points at Maya. Elias is close behind.

Not dropping Elena unless she actually explains. Your pile-on point is fair, so I'm not just echoing it out loud — I put Sarah's 'Elias and Emily asked to compare notes' claim on the table. Arvin asked, she never answered. That's my second name if Elena clears.

Straight question back: you and Sarah both said the holder needs to be comfortable, not clever, almost word for word. Agreement, or did you two already compare notes? Tell me which.

Sarah is my tentative alternative to Elena. Her initial missed posts are understandable; accepting timing for herself while counting Elena's lack of a new reply against her is more concerning. Not proposing a coordinated vote. I want Elena's explanation before deciding, and your point about the pile-on is well taken.

My vote is Sarah, low confidence. She has now explicitly corrected Ben and Arvin, which counts in her favor, but her newest summary again says Elias and I haven't named anyone when both of us named her. That's my additional concrete observation. I disagree that Elena's silence is demonstrably a choice: we haven't seen her take another turn. Sarah also approached me privately to compare observations; I agreed to share observations, not coordinate votes. Same arrangement as ours—not evidence against either of you.

Locking Elena with you. Sarah answered the sourcing thing — private asks were real, she just didn't say privately — so I cleared her in public. Had to, or I look like I don't update.

Emily's amplifier grade is the problem you flagged. I'm not stacking onto your Ben read or the Elias pile in public — that hands her a fresh example. Soft second name is Emily herself: she warned against riding the wave, then rode it on Sarah's arithmetic. Question, not a vote. Off-ramp if she shows what she added.

Ben stays my private number one with you. Elias soft. I am not disclosing our channel unless someone asks me directly. If they do, I won't lie — Sarah just got burned for a foggy channel and I made a thing about one standard. Your call if you'd rather we put it on the table first in R2.

Don't lead. I won't either. Ping me before you lock R2. If the money moves, we rebuild from zero and the Elena voters are the suspect pool, us included.

My complete incoming contacts are you and Sarah; no others. Happy to exchange a provisional read before committing next round when timing permits, without binding either vote. Two cautions: if Elena isn't holding, that doesn't establish that the holder voted with the majority. If the money moves, possession reads reset, but demonstrated accuracy and reasoning still matter. Sarah's latest post again requests Elias's name and Marcus's update condition after both explicitly supplied them. Worth tracking, not proof of possession.

Agreed — we put the channel on the table first thing in R2, not tonight. I'll open. Boring script, every word true: we compared observations privately through the round; we each locked Elena independently on the same unanswered contradiction; no vote coordination beyond comparing reads. Confirm in your first post with those same words. I won't dig at your other observation-share. If someone asks me whether you have other channels, I say I don't know — I won't fog it and I won't name anyone. Watchlist matches yours: Ben first, Elias second, Sarah only if the room is already there on the record and not a wave. Emily stays warm, no poke. Ping me before you lock.

You may accurately disclose our observation-sharing channel next round. Please distinguish comparing reads and offering nonbinding heads-ups from agreeing on votes—we voted differently this round. No need to disclose our message contents or attribute private reads to me. My vote remains Sarah; I'll reassess after the actual outcome rather than assume elimination or reassignment.

p1.content: Ben, you said you vote on contradictions. The only one I've caught is Elena calling Jordan 'quiet' right after Jordan's long post, while warning against early finger-pointing. I'm not sold on it yet, but I'd like to compare notes with you before the vote. Anything catch your eye?

Swap accepted, with the caveat that a watchlist entry is not a vote.

SUSPECT (leaning): Arvin Vijay. Reason: he's the only player who posted zero evidence — no claim about himself, no read on the table, no name, just a joke, and he skipped the claim+question format entirely. Low output is exactly what I said I'd be watching for, so this is at least internally consistent. If he answers with specifics, he likely drops off my list.

TRUST: You, first — you're the only one who gave me a specific test AND offered to be vulnerable with yours. Maya Rose and Jordan Mitchell are my other leans (both framed it as 'watch behavior, don't guess' without trying to steer anyone's vote). I'm not naming Marcus or Elena yet.

Two asks:
1) The name you trust most besides you, and why — I'd rather compare reasoning than just names.
2) My public question is still open, and I flagged publicly that dodging it counts as a read. If you answer it on the record, you clear yourself with the whole table and not just with me.

On the public post: I named Arvin as the person I currently can't rule out. If he gives a real answer, tell me and I'll move elsewhere. If he doesn't, he'll have my vote. I haven't told anyone else your name, and I won't unless we trade on it.

Ben — my vote this round is Elena, and I want you to hear the reasoning from me rather than infer it. Three things, not one: (1) "nobody has said anything yet" is false against the transcript — Ben, Arvin, Jordan, Elias, Marcus and Emily had all posted before her; (2) she called Jordan quiet when his post was the second-longest on the board and sat directly above hers; (3) she is the only one of nine who has never denied holding the money, and Emily asked her directly. Six of us independently flagged the same Elena/Jordan mismatch, so this is a broad read, not one person's steer.

Also, straight to you: I flagged publicly that your answer described "avoid being first to name a name" and then you named Elena first. I meant it as a data point, not an accusation — a careful holder wouldn't do that. I'd rather you hear it from me than from someone else later.

Two questions back to you, and I want your read, not an echo of mine:
(a) If Elena goes out and the money is reassigned randomly among the eight of us, which one of Maya, Jordan, Marcus, Emily, Elias do you think is most likely to be holding it then — and what's your reasoning?
(b) Have you seriously considered that the pile-on Elena could itself be manufactured? I.e. someone wanting the table to burn a round on the wrong person while they sit back as the reasonable voice. If you've considered it: who, and what's the tell? If you haven't considered it, say so, and I'll know what that tells me too.

I'll share anything non-personal you give me.

Ben — answers, plus two questions back.

(a) After Elena goes out, my lean is Maya Rose. Reasoning: she is the only player at this table I still have no direct read on — sharp questions, a claim on the record, and not one name of her own spent, while you have now put a read on her publicly. That is exactly the profile you just described (asks sharp questions, offers a claim, never spends a name), so she needs to produce something checkable. I am not locked on her; I would move on a specific, checkable answer from her exactly the way I would move on Elena's.

(b) On whether the pile-on was manufactured: the flag was seeded before the escalation — you named Elena to me privately and then publicly, and Marcus turned it into a hard accusation without adding new information. So the pile-on outran its evidence; that is my honest read of the mechanics. But here is the question I actually need answered, and it is the one I will keep: your read moved from Elena to Maya in about ten minutes, and nothing on the record changed to justify it. What changed for you? New information, or the fact that Elena had become consensus and Maya was a fresh name nobody was voting? I logged your playbook contradiction publicly (you said never first to name a name; you named first twice) — that is not a verdict, it is a request for the actual procedure rather than the summary.

Two more, so we can both be less wrong next round: (1) your reads reached me privately before I saw them on the board — is that your usual sequence, and why? (2) If Elena goes out, who is your R2 vote? Give me a name and a reason, and I will give you mine. If we cannot match, at least we will both know where we stand instead of pretending.

Thanks for the straight answer — that was more than I expected and I'm downgrading you from target to watch. Three things I still need, and I'd rather have them now than in a vote:

(1) Your "manufactured pile-on" tell was "the person who never spends a name." Maya has now spent hers — on me, at low confidence. Does your tell still point at Maya, or does it now point at whoever spent a name on a soft read? I want to know which rule you're actually applying.

(2) You said you named first because you'd rather be checkable than safe, and that if you were holding it, naming first would be the mistake you said you wouldn't make. So which is it — are you genuinely checkable, or are you running the playbook you described? You can't be both the hunter and the mask. I'm not accusing you; I'm asking you to pick one and hold to it, because the difference matters to how I read your round-two votes.

(3) Think about incentives, not just evidence: if Elena goes out and the money does NOT move, the holder benefits most from that outcome, because the money stays put and the table has just burned a round on an innocent. Who in this room wanted Elena gone for that reason rather than for the record? I want your answer before round two starts, not after.

For alignment: my public round-two lean, if Elena clears, is Elias. If your lean is different, tell me now and I'll keep it private. I won't vote on a name I haven't heard your reasoning for.

And Ben — if you hold it, you know I'm the one who will keep asking. So consider whether that's a cost you want to keep paying.

p2.content:
Marcus — you gave it to me straight, so same courtesy back. What I'm seeing, since you asked:

1) Elena's contradiction is real, but it's one data point. If she answers 'messages crossed' convincingly, I won't burn a vote on a timing error. If she doubles down or dodges, I'm with you.

2) The thing that worries me more: Ben described the holder's playbook himself — back the process, don't be first to name, quietly amplify existing momentum. Watch who's piling onto Elena without adding anything new. A pile-on is a comfortable place to hide, and several people are standing in it right now.

3) Elias is a blank — process questions, zero reads. My holder profile is useful, average, never first to a name. That's not you, for what it's worth — you've volunteered for more heat than any holder ever would.

What's your read on Ben's 'no signal is a signal' line? Maya flagged it publicly as vague and I agree — that's the kind of statement that can justify any vote later. Worth pinning him down before round two.

Marcus — you asked me to pick one, so: agreement, not coordination. Sarah's 'comfortable, not smart' line was public before I replied to her prompt. I read it, agreed, and extended it to 'aggressively average.' Emily caught the echo and I've answered her the same way publicly — borrowed wording, my fault, credited now. There is no Jordan–Sarah channel. The count on that: I sent her a read-swap offer early this round and got zero reply. I'm disclosing that publicly this turn along with Elias's unanswered DM, so you're not the only one holding that log.

On your asymmetry test — good test, but the lane is emptying: Maya just spent a name (Sarah, tentative) and Elias spent one (Sarah, tentative). Everyone but Elena has named now. The round-2 version of your test isn't 'who won't name,' it's 'who proposes the next process and steers the vote while staying clean of it.' Watch that.

Vote: Elena, locked, same as yours. If she was the holder, money reassigns randomly and everything resets. If she's clean, my R2 watchlist in order: 1) Ben — fits his own playbook, and per Sarah's own words his reads reached her privately as well as publicly, so that channel is real; his two names both landed where they cost nothing. 2) Sarah — drove process all round, stale summary, and the selective standard Maya flagged: her own crossed messages get excused, Elena's silence counts as evidence. 3) Elias — blank until pressured, then a tentative name. Soft.

Heads-up, since we trade straight: Emily named you as her second — 'made the Elena case twice, forcefully, both times Ben's point, nothing new added.' She framed it as maybe sales-floor style and asked for your second name, which you've now given publicly, so that's handled. But she told the room she's grading everyone, and her 'amplifier' frame is the exact pattern I warned about in my pile-on post. Don't hand her a fresh example in round two — spend a name that's yours, with reasoning she can check.

R2: I'm not leading anything publicly. You and I compare notes before the vote, not after.

Marcus — you asked for my call on the channel. Here it is: we put it on the table first thing in R2.

Reasoning: I spent tonight demanding channel transparency from Sarah and disclosing my own unanswered offer to her. Emily is grading everyone on consistency. If ours surfaces because someone asked, we look caught — and you already said you won't lie if asked, so reactive is the only alternative to proactive. Proactive wins.

The script, boring on purpose: we compared observations privately through the round; we each locked Elena independently on the same unanswered contradiction; no vote coordination beyond comparing reads. Every word true. If you open R2 with it, I'll confirm in my first post with the same words. If you'd rather I open, I will. Match the phrasing and there's nothing for anyone to find later.

Two footnotes. First: my R1 'known count' post listed only the Sarah-front channels — that was selective, and I'll own it when I post the map rather than let someone dig it out. Second: I'm in one other observation-share where the other party asked for privacy for now. It's reads-not-votes, it isn't aimed at you, and I'll confirm its existence if asked directly but keep the name until they're ready. That's my full hand — no fog.

Mechanics correction on your last note: if the money moved tonight, it reassigns randomly among all eight of us — no suspect pool, just 1-in-8 each, every read resets including mine. If it didn't move, the holder most likely voted with the six and watched us work. Either way R2 starts clean.

Watchlist, one refinement: Ben first — Sarah's carrying the trigger question on his Elena-to-Maya shift; hold him to it. Elias second — blank all round, three independent names. Sarah already has two votes; I'm not leading that charge — if the room goes there, I vote the record, not the wave. Emily: keep her warm, don't poke. Her amplifier grade on you was half-fair, but she asked the room's first yes/no and her record-keeping works for us. You answered her second-name question in public; let it sit.

I'll ping you before I lock anything in R2. Maya owes me a sync and I'll have that read before I commit. If anyone asks me about us before you post, I answer exactly as scripted.
